sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines the testing 
 procedure P1, which must be performed about twice weekly as indicated by 
 W2 in the above title 
 block

The BOD test is essentially a bioassay procedure involving the measurement of 
oxygen consumed by living organisms (mainly bacteria) while utilizing organic 
matter present in waste, under conditions as similar as possible to those that 
occur in natural.
Significance

The BOD test is widely used to determine the pollutional strength of domestic 
and industrial wastes in terms of the oxygen that they will required if 
discharged into natural watercourses in which aerobic conditions exist. This 
test is of prime importance in regulatory work and in studies designed to 
evaluate the purification capacity of receiving bodies of water.
Definition

Biochemical Oxygen 
 Demand is defined as the amount of oxygen required by bacteria while 
 stabilizing decomposable organic matter under aerobic conditions.

The test has been 
 developed on the basis of 5-days incubation period because it has been found 
 by experience that a reasonably large percentage of the total BOD ( 70 to 80 
 %) is exerted in 5-days and it is also selected to minimized interference from 
 oxidation of ammonia.

items:
Clean the bottles by use of chromic acid or a good grade of 
 detergent.

The bottles must be rinsed with hot water to kill 
 nitrifying organism, then the bottles are rinsed four times with tap water and 
 a final rinse with distilled or demineralized water.

Collect surface water samples in narrow- mouth glass 
 stopper BOD bottles 300 mL.

Sampling from a line under pressure attached a glass or 
 rubber tube to the tap and extend to bottom of bottle, let bottle overflow two or three times its volume and replace so that no air bubbles are 
 entrained.

sections.text: Safety Precautions

items: The sample must be kept away from direct sunlight.
Make sure the sample bottles is correctly labeled.

Make sure the sample bottles is free from dust and organic 
 matter.

The bottles used for BOD should be equipped with glass 
 stopper that are ground to a point to prevent trapping of air when the stopper 
 is inserted.

The bottles must be equipped with some of water seal to 
 prevent air from entering the bottle during the incubation period.

Interference of reducing and oxidizing material are masked 
 by low pH value used and addition of NaN3.

sections.text: Two 300 ml BOD Bottle, Pipettes (2mL- 3mL- 5mL).
Reagents

Manganous Sulfate Solution-Dissolve 
 364g of manganous sulfate MnSO4.H2O in distilled 
 water, and dilute to1 liter.

Alkali-Iodide, 
 Azide Reagent-Dissolve 500g of sodium hydroxide NaOH and 135g NaI
 in distilled water and dilute to 1 liter. Add 10g NaN3 dissolved in 
 40mL distilled
 water

Sodium 
 ThioSulfate Standard Solution (0.025M)-Dissolve 6.025g of Na2S2O3.5H2O in distilled water. Standardize with Bi-Iodate solution.

Standard 
 Potassium Bi-Iodate Solution (0.0021M)-Dissolve 
 812.4mg KH(IO3)2 in distilled water, and dilute 
 to1 liter.

Starch Solution-
 Use either an aqueous solution or a soluble starch powder mixtures.

Sulfuric Acid -Concentrated 
 sulfuric acid H2SO4 one milliliter is equivalent to about 
 3mL Alkali-Iodide, Azide Reagent.
Standardization

items:
Dissolve approximately 2g KI free from iodate in flask with 100mL to 150mL distilled water, add 1mL 
 (6N) H2SO4 or few drops of conc. H2SO4 
 and 20mL Standard Bi-Iodate solution.

Dilute to 200mL and 
 titrate librated iodine with thiosulfate titrant adding starch toward the end 
 of titration when pale straw color is reached. When the solutions are of equal 
 strength, 20mL (0.025M) Na2S2O3 
 should be required if not adjust the Na2S2O3 
 solution to (0.025M).

sections.text: Work To be Carried Out
Procedure

Filled 
 two or more BOD bottles with sample at least one is analyzed for dissolved oxygen 
 immediately at power station by fixation with manganous sulfate and sodium 
 azide, and the others are incubated for 5-days at 20oC.

Determine 
 the amount of dissolved oxygen remaining in the incubated samples after 
 5-days, as shown in the dissolved oxygen test.

sections.text: Calculation

Calculate 
 the 5-days BOD by subtracting of 5-days results from those obtained on 
 day 0.

BOD in mg/l = 
 Doi - Dof
Where:

Doi 
 = Dissolved Oxygen initial at zero day,

Dof 
 = Dissolved Oxygen final after 5 days.
